title: An improved method for extraction of soil fungal mycelium
author: Awad, Pena
materials: Genomic DNA was isolated from freeze-dried samples of soil-extracted mycelium using the Innu PREP Plant DNA kit (Analytik Jena, Jena, Germany) according to the manufacturer's protocol. Internal transcribed spacer (ITS) fungal rDNA region was amplified using the fungal-specific pair of the forward ITS1F (CTTGGTCATTTAGAGGAAGTAA) and reverse ITS4 (TCCTCCGCTTATTGATATGC) primers [38]. To check for positive amplification, 3.0 µl of the PCR products were mixed with 0.5 µL DNA loading dye GelRed (Biotium, Inc., Fremont, CA), loaded on 1.5 % agarose gel in TAE(Tris-acetate-EDTA) buffer, at 120 Vs for 35 min, and visualised under UV light (Fluor-STM multi-imager; Bio-Rad, Munich, Germany). A DNA ladder solution (Biotium, Inc., Fremont, CA) and positive and negative controls were also loaded in the gel to estimate the size of PCR products and for reference.

steps.title: Collect and homogenize soil samples
steps.instruction: In each of the 27 100 × 100 m plots (Alb 7, Hai 10, Sch 10) collect seven soil cores (0.08 m diameter, 0.10 m depth) along two 40 m transects after removing the surface organic layer; combine cores per plot, sieve through a 2 mm mesh, remove visible root fragments, take a 10.0 g aliquot, split into two 5.0 g portions, and store at –20 °C.

substeps.instruction: Collect seven soil cores per plot (0.08 m diameter, 0.10 m depth) along two 40 m transects after removing the surface organic layer
Combine cores per plot, sieve through 2 mm mesh and remove visible root fragments
Take 10.0 g aliquot, split into two 5.0 g portions, store at –20 °C

steps.title: Optional removal of root fragments
steps.instruction: Under a stereomicroscope, use tweezers to pick out remaining root fragments and plant debris from the 5.0 g soil portion before extraction.

steps.title: Disperse soil in deionised water
steps.instruction: Place 5.0 g soil in 100 ml deionised water and stir with a bar stir on an IKA Kombimag® RCT magnetic stirrer at 500 rpm for 5.0 min.

steps.title: First filtration through 1000 µm mesh
steps.instruction: Filter the suspension twice through a 1000 µm nylon mesh cloth (Franz Eckert GmbH), washing the retained oversize particles with an additional 100 ml deionised water.

substeps.instruction: Filter suspension twice through 1000 µm nylon mesh
Wash retained particles with 100 ml deionised water

steps.title: Second filtration and collect oversize particles
steps.instruction: Filter the resulting liquid twice through a metal sieve of 50.0 µm pore size padded with a 50.0 µm nylon mesh; discard the filtrate and collect the retained oversize particles (bulk mycelial stock) into a 50 ml Falcon tube by gently adding 25.0 ml deionised water with a pipette.

substeps.instruction: Filter filtrate twice through 50 µm metal sieve padded with 50 µm nylon mesh
Discard filtrate
Collect oversize particles into 50 ml Falcon tube using 25 ml deionised water added with a pipette

steps.title: Cold pre‑centrifugation and supernatant removal
steps.instruction: Keep the Falcon tubes at 4 °C for several hours, then centrifuge for 3.0 min at 3100 × g using an Eppendorf 5810R; verify under a microscope that no hyphae remain in the supernatant and discard the supernatant.

substeps.instruction: Incubate tubes at 4 °C for several hours
Centrifuge 3 min at 3100 × g (Eppendorf 5810R)
Discard supernatant after confirming absence of hyphae

steps.title: Sucrose gradient washes (repeat five times)
steps.instruction: Vigorously hand‑shake the pellet into 50.0 ml of 45.5 % (w/v) sucrose solution, centrifuge at 50 × g for 1.0 min, collect the supernatant and pipette it onto a three‑layered 50.0 µm nylon mesh; repeat the dispersion, centrifugation, and supernatant collection five times total, then discard the final pellet.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend pellet in 50 ml 45.5 % sucrose solution
Centrifuge 1 min at 50 × g
Collect supernatant onto 50 µm nylon mesh
Repeat the three actions five times total
Discard final pellet

steps.title: Wash mesh and recover mycelium
steps.instruction: Rinse the mesh thoroughly with deionised water until all sucrose is removed, then carefully scrape the retained particles from the mesh into a 2.0 ml Eppendorf tube.

substeps.instruction: Rinse mesh with deionised water until sucrose removed
Scrape retained particles into 2 ml Eppendorf tube

steps.title: Freeze‑dry mycelium for DNA extraction
steps.instruction: Freeze‑dry the collected mycelium fraction before DNA isolation.

steps.title: Extract genomic DNA with plant kit
steps.instruction: Isolate genomic DNA from the freeze‑dried mycelium using the Innu PREP Plant DNA kit (Analytik Jena, Jena, Germany) following the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Amplify fungal ITS region by PCR
steps.instruction: Perform PCR with fungal‑specific primers ITS1F (CTTGGTCATTTAGAGGAAGTAA) and ITS4 (TCCTCCGCTTATTGATATGC) to amplify the internal transcribed spacer region.

steps.title: Verify PCR products via agarose gel
steps.instruction: Mix 3.0 µl of each PCR product with 0.5 µl GelRed loading dye, load onto a 1.5 % agarose gel prepared in TAE buffer, run at 120 V for 35 min, and visualize bands under UV light using a Bio‑Rad Fluor‑STM imager; include a DNA ladder and positive/negative controls.

substeps.instruction: Mix 3 µl PCR product with 0.5 µl GelRed
Load onto 1.5 % agarose gel in TAE buffer
Run at 120 V for 35 min
Visualize under UV with ladder and controls

description: Relative extraction efficiency (%) of soil mycelium, when the initial soil represented 100 % recovery, was estimated to 49.6 ± 3.5 % in Alb, 50.6 ± 2.3 % in Hai, and 22.5 ± 1.1 % in Sch soil samples. These results are in the range of those obtained by Bingle and Paul [30], who used glycerol density gradient centrifugation to obtain soil particle-free hyphae. Although the total hyphal length measured in the initial soil did not vary between soils of the three regions (Fig. 2), the hyphal length of extracted mycelium was significantly higher in the clay soils of Alb and Hai than in loamy sand soils of Sch (Fig. 2). In Alb soil, extracted mycelium, mean hyphal length value was about 110 m g−1, while in Hai soil was 80 m g−1 following the trend of a higher amount of clay found in Alb soils (496 g kg−1) compared with Hai soils (301 g kg−1, Table 1, [40]).Fig. 2Hyphal length in the initial soil from where the mycelium was extracted, extracted mycelium, and discarded soil pellet at the end of the procedure. Soil samples were collected in three regions, Swabian Alb (Alb), Hainich-Dün (Hai), and Schorfheide-Chorin (Sch). Uppercase letters represent the statistical differences between the hyphal lengths of extracted mycelium; Lowercase letters represent the statistical differences between the hyphal lengths of discarded soil residues (n = 7 for Alb, n = 10 for Hai, and Sch).Fig 2 To recover the values found in the initial soil, hyphal lengths were measured in all discarded and collected fractions in the mycelium extraction procedure. However, hyphal measurement was not achievable in the oversize particle fraction in step 4 (1000 µm filtration, Fig. 1), which contained numerous root fragments rich in fungal structures of mycorrhizal root tips or pieces of the ectomycorrhizal mantle, and soil or sand particles carrying an unspecific amount of hyphae (Fig. 3a and b).
